findings.issue_text: RSS/Atom feed content is imported via TopicEmbed.import with cook_method: raw_html, causing Post#cook to skip Discourse's sanitize pipeline and render raw feed HTML via `raw post.cooked`, enabling stored XSS from a malicious/compromised feed

TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read without validating the URL scheme, unlike TopicEmbed.import; since Kernel#open treats leading '|' as a shell command, this allows command injection via crafted URLs (including from lib/tasks/disqus.thor)

TopicEmbed.import performs a non-atomic check-then-create on embed_url, so concurrent callers can both pass the blank? check and both call create!, causing an unhandled RecordNotUnique/RecordInvalid due to the unique index on embed_url

PollFeed's CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) assumes every feed item has a content field; plain RSS 2.0 items without content:encoded have i.content == nil, raising NoMethodError and aborting the entire hourly poll run since retries are disabled

embed.js uses document.getElementById('discourse-comments') without checking for null, so a missing element causes comments.appendChild(iframe) to throw and can break the rest of the host page's script execution

embed.js checks discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 to validate message origin, which is a substring check rather than an equality check, allowing origins that merely contain a matching substring to pass

embed_controller.rb relies solely on the client-supplied Referer header to restrict access, which is attacker-controlled and doesn't reliably prevent arbitrary URLs from triggering Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)

No tests cover TopicEmbed.import_remote (the open(url)/Readability path) or the actual body of Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed (RSS parsing and per-item import), leaving the sanitization gap in finding #1 uncovered
The --category/-c option and its logic for assigning imported threads to a category were removed from lib/tasks/disqus.thor with no replacement, silently changing behavior for existing users

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: RSS/Atom feed content is imported via TopicEmbed.import with cook_method: raw_html, causing Post#cook to skip Discourse's sanitize pipeline and render raw feed HTML via `raw post.cooked`, enabling stored XSS from a malicious/compromised feed

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff explicitly introduces a “raw_html” cook method that bypasses the normal cooking/rendering pipeline: `Post#cook` now does `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, skipping `post_analyzer.cook` (which is where Discourse’s normal markdown/HTML sanitization would occur). Feed importing uses this mode: `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts via `PostCreator.new(... raw: absolutize_urls(url, contents), skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`. The embed view then renders the post content with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. In the RSS poller (`Jobs::PollFeed`), `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` is taken from the feed and passed into `TopicEmbed.import` with no sanitization (and `absolutize_urls` only rewrites relative href/src; it does not remove scripts/handlers). This combination allows untrusted feed HTML to be stored and later rendered as raw HTML, which is a verifiable stored XSS risk if the feed is malicious/compromised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import_remote calls open(url).read without validating the URL scheme, unlike TopicEmbed.import; since Kernel#open treats leading '|' as a shell command, this allows command injection via crafted URLs (including from lib/tasks/disqus.thor)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which does `open(url).read` on an unvalidated `url` parameter. Unlike `TopicEmbed.import`, it does not restrict to `http/https` (or otherwise sanitize). In Ruby, `Kernel#open` (used by open-uri) treats strings beginning with `|` as a command to execute (popen), and also allows non-HTTP schemes (e.g., `file:`), so this is a real security/correctness issue in the new code. The diff also introduces a concrete caller (`lib/tasks/disqus.thor`) that passes `t[:link]` into `import_remote` without validation, making the risk present in the changed code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import performs a non-atomic check-then-create on embed_url, so concurrent callers can both pass the blank? check and both call create!, causing an unhandled RecordNotUnique/RecordInvalid due to the unique index on embed_url

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, it does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then, if `embed.blank?`, it enters a transaction and eventually calls `TopicEmbed.create!(..., embed_url: url, ...)`. Because there is a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` (migration `add_index :topic_embeds, :embed_url, unique: true`), two concurrent callers can both observe `embed.blank?` and both attempt `create!`; the second will raise (typically `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`, possibly surfaced as `StatementInvalid` depending on adapter). There is no rescue/handling in this method, so the exception would bubble and fail the import job/request. The surrounding `Topic.transaction` does not prevent this race without locking or an atomic upsert.

matched_golden_ids: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden and candidate comments identify the same underlying bug: the code calls `i.content.scrub` (and further processing) assuming `i.content` is always present, but many RSS items lack a `content`/`content:encoded` field so `i.content` can be nil, causing a NoMethodError/nil dereference. The golden suggests falling back to `description`; the candidate describes the same failure mode and context.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js uses document.getElementById('discourse-comments') without checking for null, so a missing element causes comments.appendChild(iframe) to throw and can break the rest of the host page's script execution

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, it does `var comments = document.getElementById('discourse-comments')` and then immediately calls `comments.appendChild(iframe);` with no null/undefined guard. If the host page includes this script but does not have an element with id `discourse-comments`, `comments` will be `null` and `appendChild` will throw a runtime exception, aborting execution of this embed script (and potentially impacting other JS error handling on the host page). This is a concrete, directly verifiable defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js checks discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1 to validate message origin, which is a substring check rather than an equality check, allowing origins that merely contain a matching substring to pass
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both the golden and candidate identify that origin validation uses indexOf/substring matching instead of strict equality, which can be bypassed by malicious origins containing the expected URL as a substring (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com).

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb relies solely on the client-supplied Referer header to restrict access, which is attacker-controlled and doesn't reliably prevent arbitrary URLs from triggering Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)

adjudication.rationale:
In EmbedController#ensure_embeddable, authorization is based on `request.referer` host matching `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`:

```rb
raise ... if URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host
```

`Referer` is a client-supplied header and can be trivially spoofed by a non-browser client (or any attacker making direct HTTP requests). If an attacker supplies a forged Referer with the allowed host, the controller will proceed and, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, will enqueue `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` without validating that `embed_url` itself matches the allowed host.

While `TopicRetriever` later has a host check (`invalid_host?` compares `URI(@embed_url).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`), the finding is still verifiable as written: the controller’s gate relies solely on an attacker-controlled Referer, and arbitrary `embed_url` values can still cause the enqueue to happen (even if the job later no-ops).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests cover TopicEmbed.import_remote (the open(url)/Readability path) or the actual body of Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed (RSS parsing and per-item import), leaving the sanitization gap in finding #1 uncovered

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new behavior in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (fetching remote HTML via `open(url).read` and extracting content with `Readability::Document`) and in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (fetching/parsing a feed via `SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and importing each item). The added specs cover `TopicEmbed.import` (not `import_remote`) and `Jobs::PollFeed#execute` gating logic only (it never calls/validates the RSS parsing or per-item import logic). Therefore, it is verifiably true that these new code paths are not directly tested in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The --category/-c option and its logic for assigning imported threads to a category were removed from lib/tasks/disqus.thor with no replacement, silently changing behavior for existing users

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor, the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` line was removed, along with the code that looked up `category_id` from `options[:category]` and passed it into `PostCreator.new(..., category: category_id)`. The import path now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, which does not accept or set a category in this diff. This is a clear behavior/API change: existing users/scripts that relied on `--category/-c` to import into a specific category will no longer be able to do so, and the change is silent (no deprecation or alternative shown here).
